I found no prediction about AI from Mustafa Suleyman in 2013. The three fixed searches each ran once, plus five more aimed at that year. Nothing turned up in his own words from 2013, and nothing that names a date or time span. That fits the context: DeepMind kept a low profile until December 2013, when it staged a kind of debutante moment at a leading research conference on machine learning.

What turned up instead:
- **Later retellings of 2013.** In recent interviews Suleyman mentions 2013 as the year DeepMind trained its AI on Atari games (the Jordan Harbinger interview and the Diary of a CEO transcript). These are things he said in later years about the past, not predictions made in 2013. I only saw them in search snippets and didn't open the pages.
- **The earliest piece in his own words I found is from 2015.** I opened his Edge essay "General Purpose Learning Machines." The page files it under Edge's 2015 question, "What do you think about machines that think?", so I've listed it under other years. I didn't check it closely for dated predictions.
- **Everything else is from 2016 onward.** One item is a Hacker News thread, apparently from 2016, about him saying general AI is "still a long way off." The rest runs from 2023 to now: the 2023 book "The Coming Wave," his talk about AI that could act like an entrepreneur within five years, and the "12 to 18 months" white-collar automation remark.

Two calls failed because of a parsing bug in my own code, not a problem with the sites. I printed the first search's results from memory afterwards rather than running it again, so every search ran once. In total I used 8 of 12 searches and 1 of 6 page openings.
